newsitem.title: USA: US Airways to buy back shrs from BA.
newsitem.headline: US Airways to buy back shrs from BA.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc said Tuesday it will repurchase most of the US Airways preferred stock held by British Airways Plc, which will end the turbulent relationship between the two carriers.
BA said in December it planned to sell its 24.6 percent stake in its estranged marketing partner.
Although US Airways said in February it would not exercise its right to buy back BA's stake, US Airways said it now meets the capital surplus requirements to repurchase the shares.

A Delaware capital surplus law limits share repurchases unless a comany meets certain capital surplus thresholds. A spokesman for US Airways declined to comment on the company's capital surplus level.

"We see this as a very attractive apportunity to purchase stock at a discount to current markets," said Stephen Wolf, US Airways' chairman and chief executive. "We will continue to seek opportunities to use the company's resources to increase value for our shareholders."
US Airways said it will repurchase from BA all of the outstanding Series T-1 and Series T-2 preferred stock and a portion of the Series F preferred stock.
US Airways said the purchase price for all 152.1 shares of Series T-1 preferred stock and all 9,919.8 shares of T-2 preferred share is equivalent to $26.50 a common share.
The purchase price for 1,940.6 shares of the total 30,000 shares of Series F stock is equivalent to $24.63 per common share, US Airways said.
These shares, which US Airways will retire, would be convertible into about 4.8 million shares of common stock, the company said.
British Airways has agreed to convert the remaining Series F preferred stock into common stock on or prior to June 3, 1997, US Airways said.
BA invested about $400 million in US Airways in 1993. US Airways and BA began feuding publicly last summer after BA proposed a broad alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines.

US Airways sued BA in July, alleging the proposed BA-American deal undermined the existing relationship between US Airways and BA. US Airways also contended the proposed deal would allow BA and American to monopolize air travel between the United States and Britain.
The three BA representatives on US Airways' board resigned in January.
